newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kayaba, Arvin agree on venture in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Kayaba, Arvin agree on venture in Spain.

text.p: Japanese hydraulic equipment maker Kayaba Industry Co Ltd said on Thursday it has agreed with Arvin Industries Inc of the United States to turn Kayaba's Spanish car components subsidiary into a joint venture.

Under the agreement, there will be an increase in the capital of the Spanish firm, Kayaba Spain SA, from the current 490 million pesetas to one billion pesetas on December 1. Of the new total capital, 60 percent will be held by Kayaba and the rest by Arvin, Kayaba said in a statement.
In conjunction with the capital increase, the company will also be renamed Kayaba Arvin SA, the statement said.
Kayaba set up the Spanish firm to make vane pumps for car power-steering devices in Europe.
The firm is spending 2.4 billion pesetas to build production facilities, which are expected to be completed in early 1997.
Initially, the firm expects to produce 30,000 to 40,000 vane pumps a month. It will increase monthly production to 100,000 pumps within a few years.
